text: You woke up. That's okay.

Waking in the middle of the night is one of the most natural things your body does. It happens to everyone, every night. Most of the time you fall back without remembering. Tonight, you remembered. That's all.
Let your eyes close.
Let the dark come back.
Whatever woke you, a thought, a sound, a dream, it's already fading. Let it fade.
You are safe. You are in your bed. The night is still here, and there is more sleep waiting for you.
The first thing to do is feel your body.
Feel the mattress underneath you.
Feel the pillow. Feel the covers.
Feel how warm you are.
This warmth is a sign. Your body is still in sleep mode. It's still ready.
Take a slow breath in.
And a long, soft exhale.
Again. Breathing in.
And breathing out, letting the exhale be twice as long as the inhale.
Good.
Your body wants to go back. You're helping it.
Let go of any thoughts about the time.
The clock is irrelevant right now. Whether it's midnight or four in the morning, your only job is the same. Be still. Be warm. Breathe.
If your mind is spinning, that's okay.
The mind often fires up when you wake at night. It starts listing things, worrying, planning.
Let it talk. You are choosing to listen to the breath instead.
Every time a thought pulls you, come back to the exhale.
The exhale is your anchor. It always brings you back.
Feel your body getting heavier again.
Your shoulders, sinking.
Your jaw, softening.
Your hands, still and warm.
You were asleep a few minutes ago. Your body remembers exactly how to get there.
It's like a path you've walked a thousand times. You could walk it with your eyes closed. You are walking it right now.
Let yourself drift.
Feel the pull of sleep.
It's right there, like a warm current.
Let it carry you.
Everything else can wait until morning.
Everything.
Your body is heavy.
Your breath is slow.
Your mind is getting quiet again.
Fall back in.
Fall back into sleep.
It's warm in there. It's waiting.
Goodnight. Again.
